title: U.S. House · Virginia's 7th District
area: Central and northern Virginia, stretching across eleven localities including Fredericksburg, Spotsylvania, Stafford, Culpeper and parts of Prince William County.

context.text: Incumbent Eugene Vindman won a crowded, later-uncontested Democratic primary after eight other candidates (including Dorothy McAuliffe and Olivia Troye) withdrew or were disqualified. Douglas Ollivant won the Republican primary with 56.6% over Philip Harding (30.7%) and Rick Smithers (12.7%). Vindman won the seat in 2024, defeating Derrick Anderson. Both national parties are targeting the race: the NRCC named it a target district and the DCCC placed Vindman in its Frontline program for vulnerable incumbents. Four other candidates qualified for the general-election ballot: Taner Demirci Lopez (Libertarian), Alaha Ahrar, Joshua Ertle and Randall Terry (independents).

candidates.name: Eugene Vindman
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Democratic primary unopposed after other candidates withdrew and the primary was canceled.

summary.text: Eugene Vindman is the Democratic incumbent seeking a second term representing Virginia's 7th District. A retired U.S. Army officer and former White House National Security Council attorney, he was first elected in 2024 after a 25-year Army career and work on war-crimes investigations in Ukraine. According to his campaign website, his top priority is cutting taxes and lowering costs for working families.

background.text: Came to the United States at age four with his family as refugees fleeing Soviet Ukraine and grew up in New York, attending public schools and a public university.

Earned a bachelor's degree from the State University of New York at Binghamton in 1997, a master's degree from Central Michigan University in 2005 and a law degree from the University of Georgia School of Law in 2009.

Received an Army ROTC commission as a second lieutenant and served in the Army from 1997 to 2022 as an infantry officer and paratrooper, including assignments in the 82nd Airborne Division and as a company commander.

Transitioned to the Army Judge Advocate General's (JAG) Corps, serving as an international law advisor in Iraq and as senior prosecutor in the Army's busiest jurisdiction. According to his congressional biography, he attained the rank of Colonel before retiring in 2022 after 25 years of service.
Served as a deputy legal advisor and agency ethics official on the White House National Security Council.

After retiring, spent 18 months investigating war crimes in Ukraine, making 14 trips as a senior consultant for a State Department-funded program; Ballotpedia lists him as Director of Military Analysis and Prosecution Support for the Atrocity Crimes Advisory group.
Ran for Congress in 2024 for the seat Abigail Spanberger left to run for governor; defeated Republican Derrick Anderson in the general election by 2.7 percentage points and took office in 2025.
Serves on the House Armed Services Committee and the House Agriculture Committee.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Cindy raised their son and daughter in Dale City, Virginia.

priorities.text: Lowering costs for working families and cracking down on anti-competitive business practices.
priorities.quote: is working to crack down on anti-competitive business practices, lower costs for working families, support small businesses, and ensure economic development creates opportunity in every community.

priorities.text: Banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks or participating in prediction markets, and from lobbying former colleagues after leaving office.
Protecting federal workers from political attacks and government shutdowns, and rebuilding federal agencies affected by DOGE-driven cuts.
priorities.quote: supports protecting federal workers from political attacks and reckless government shutdowns, rebuilding agencies weakened by DOGE-driven cuts and chaos, and ensuring public servants are treated with the dignity, respect, and stability they deserve.

candidates.name: Douglas Ollivant
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary with 56.6% of the vote over Philip Harding and Rick Smithers.

summary.text: Douglas Ollivant is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Eugene Vindman. A retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel with combat tours in Iraq, he later served as Director for Iraq at the National Security Council and is now managing partner of a consulting firm. His campaign has emphasized energy costs, housing supply, spending cuts and national security.

background.text: Lives in Culpeper County and previously lived in Falls Church; his campaign describes him as a husband, father of seven and grandfather of two.
Attended Wheaton College, James Madison University and Indiana University, per Ballotpedia, which lists a bachelor's degree, a master's degree and a doctorate.
Served in the U.S. Army and reached the rank of lieutenant colonel; news reports describe two combat tours in Iraq and service as an adviser of coalition forces in Afghanistan.
Taught at the U.S. Military Academy at West Point.
Served as Director for Iraq at the National Security Council under Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama.
Works as managing partner of Mantid International, LLC, a compliance and business-intelligence consulting firm that, per a news report, has offices in Washington, D.C., Guam, Beirut and Baghdad.
Won the Republican nomination for the 7th District in the August 4, 2026 primary, defeating Philip Harding and Rick Smithers.

priorities.text: Expanding energy supply through an "all-of-the-above" approach centered on small modular nuclear reactors and natural gas.
priorities.quote: Virginia's families deserve affordable energy, and our communities need reliable power they can count on. That's why I support a common sense all-of-the-above approach, with small modular nuclear reactors and natural gas at the center.

priorities.text: Increasing housing supply by reducing regulation on development and redevelopment.
priorities.quote: The best way to increase supply is to reduce regulation for development, redevelopment, and building supply chains, while creating some legal protections against frivolous zoning disputes.

priorities.text: Advancing a foreign policy focused on border security and protecting U.S. interests.

positions.summary: Says the best way to increase housing supply is to reduce regulation on development and redevelopment.
positions.quote: The best way to increase supply is to reduce regulation for development, redevelopment, and building supply chains, while creating some legal protections against frivolous zoning disputes.

summary.text: Taner Demirci Lopez is the Libertarian Party candidate for Virginia's 7th District. According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he is a scholar and former college professor who later worked as a cultural advisor to U.S. government agencies. He says he is running on restoring national independence, reducing federal spending and taxation, and reforming immigration policy.

background.text: Describes himself as a U.S. citizen raised in a multicultural family who studied Spanish language and literature.
Earned a master's degree in Religions and Cultures and a doctorate in Theology from the University of Murcia in Spain, leading to a career as a scholar and college professor, according to his survey.
Says he later left academia to work as a cultural advisor supporting several U.S. government agencies.
Says he joined the Libertarian Party because he believes the two-party system has failed to represent Americans.

priorities.text: Reducing the influence of lobbyists, corporations and foreign interests on government, and cutting federal taxation and spending.

summary.text: Alaha Ahrar is an independent candidate on the general-election ballot for Virginia's 7th District. Ballotpedia lists no campaign profile or key messages for her, and FEC filings show minimal campaign activity ($115 in receipts as of June 30, 2026).
Joshua Ertle is an independent candidate on the general-election ballot for Virginia's 7th District. Ballotpedia lists no campaign profile, key messages, or campaign finance activity for him.

Randall Terry is an independent candidate on the general-election ballot for Virginia's 7th District. He is the founder of the anti-abortion group Operation Rescue and has run for office in several earlier races. Ballotpedia lists no campaign profile, key messages or campaign finance activity for him in this race.

background.text: Born in 1959; Ballotpedia lists education at Elim Bible Institute (1981) and Whitfield College (1995).
Founded Operation Rescue, an anti-abortion organization, and led it until 1991.

Ran for Congress in Upstate New York in 1998 and for the Florida Senate in 2006, losing the Republican primary both times; ran in the 2012 Democratic presidential primaries and as an independent for Florida's 20th District that year.
Was the Constitution Party's nominee for president in 2024.
Ballotpedia also lists him as a withdrawn or disqualified candidate for New Jersey's 7th District in 2026; he will not appear on that ballot.

researchNotes: Ollivant's own campaign website was not independently fetched; his priorities and quotes are drawn from Ballotpedia's staff-curated candidate profile, which cites and quotes his campaign website. Ahrar, Ertle and Terry have no public campaign materials found beyond their ballot listing and minimal FEC filings. Biography gaps: no biographical details were found for Ahrar or Ertle, and Ollivant's Army service dates are omitted because the dates listed by Ballotpedia could not be reconciled with news reports of his rank and combat tours.
